'''''Acokanthera oblongifolia''''' (commonly known as '''African wintersweet''', '''dune poison bush''', '''Hottentot's poison''', '''poison arrow plant''' or '''wintersweet'''<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | ''Acokanthera oblongifolia'' | 102583 | accessdate = 8 August 2017 }}</ref>) is a plant in the family [[Apocynaceae]].<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77164695-1 |title= Acokanthera oblongifolia (Hochst.) Benth. & Hook.f. ex B.D.Jacks. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=December 13, 2024}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/9FRH |title= Acokanthera oblongifolia (Hochst.) Benth. & Hook.f. ex B.D.Jacks. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=December 13, 2024}}</ref> It grows as an evergreen shrub or small tree up to {{convert|6|m}} tall. Its fragrant flowers feature a white tinged pink [[Corolla (flower)|corolla]]. The berries are purple when ripe. Its habitat is dry forest and coastal thickets. ''Acokanthera oblongifolia'' is used in local African medicinal treatments for snakebites, itches and internal worms. The plant has been used as [[arrow poison]].<ref name=Med>{{cite book | title = Medicinal Plants | publisher = PROTA | year= 2008 | pages = 29–30 | isbn = 978-9-05782-204-9}}</ref> The species is native to [[Mozambique]] and [[South Africa]].<ref name=WCSP/><ref name=Med/>

==Taxonomy==
It was first described in 1844 by [[Christian Ferdinand Friedrich Hochstetter]] as ''Carissa oblongifolia,''<ref name=ipni/><ref name=hochst/> reassigned in 1876 to the genus, ''[[Acokanthera]]'', by George Bentham and Joseph Hooker,<ref name=hooker>{{cite journal|url=https://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/657858|date=1876|author=Bentham, G.|author2=Hooker, J.D.|journal=Genera Plantarum :ad Exemplaria Imprimis in Herberiis Kewensibus Servata Definita|volume=2|issue=2|page=696|title=Apocynaceae}}</ref> but not validly, and finally, in 1895, validly published by [[Benjamin Daydon Jackson]]  as ''Acokanthera oblongifolia''.<ref name=ipni/><ref name=jacks/>
